2026-09-08T03:25:08.8344312Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8344884Z 
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8345255Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8345760Z 
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8346244Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8346755Z 
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8348351Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8350524Z >
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8352836Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8355231Z >
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8356032Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8356791Z 
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8356969Z ### How to Use
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8357210Z 
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8358025Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8358953Z 
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8359140Z ```bash
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8359726Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8360468Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8361098Z ```
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8361312Z 
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8361574Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8362126Z ```bash
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8362954Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8363787Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8364649Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8365398Z ```
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8365614Z 
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8366251Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8367139Z ```bash
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8367710Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8368394Z ```
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8379918Z 
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8380628Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8381308Z ```bash
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8381881Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8382791Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8383508Z ```
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8383721Z 
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8383998Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8384437Z 
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8385836Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8387416Z 
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8387594Z ```bash
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8388047Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8389222Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8390114Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8390433Z 
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8390911Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8391923Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8392752Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8393220Z ```
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8393462Z 
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8394218Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8395124Z 
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8395299Z ```bash
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8395986Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8396876Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8397596Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8398044Z 
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8398441Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8399823Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8400412Z ```
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8400619Z 
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8400841Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8401682Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8409084Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8410135Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8411182Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8412426Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8413604Z 
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8413812Z ### Notes
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8414052Z 
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8417605Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8419432Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8420728Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8423223Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8425793Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8427023Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8428035Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8428977Z </mcp-clis>
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8429394Z <github-context>
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8430012Z The following GitHub context information is available for this workflow:

2026-09-08T03:25:08.8442030Z # hn-daily-digest
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8442281Z 
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8442464Z ## Instructions
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8442704Z 
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8444197Z Create a daily digest workflow for professional developers, referencing
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8445128Z relevant top Hacker News stories on technology that can be used today
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8446008Z by large companies. Every weekday, fetch the top 30 stories from the
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8446902Z Hacker News API (https://hacker-news.firebaseio.com/v0/topstories.json),
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8447785Z filter to stories with a score above 100 that are about software
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8448787Z engineering, cloud infrastructure, AI/ML, developer tooling, or
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8449656Z distributed systems. For each qualifying story include: the title, the
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8450533Z URL, the score, the number of comments, and a one-sentence summary of
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8451894Z why it is relevant to enterprise developers. Create a GitHub issue
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8452842Z titled "HN Digest – <date>" with the results formatted as a Markdown
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8453523Z table.
2026-09-08T03:25:08.8453736Z
